# Subscription Models and Value Propositions: Notion, Evernote, and Todoist

A comparative analysis of sampled US App Store reviews reveals distinct user experiences and monetization friction points across Notion, Evernote, and Todoist. [S2](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S2) [S3](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S3) [S4](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S4) [S40](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S40)

Evernote faces significant user pushback regarding steep price increases and intrusive upgrade prompts. [S5](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S5) [S7](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S7) [S8](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S8) [S10](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S10) [S12](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S12)

Notion users report subscription management friction when billing is handled through Apple in-app purchases. [S6](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S6) [S11](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S11)

Todoist receives praise for its generous free tier, with highly-rated reviews emphasizing its organizational utility. [S20](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S20) [S24](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S24) [S31](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S31)

## Subscription and Paywall Complaints

In the pooled sample of 300 reviews across the three apps, 18 reviews matched the keyword 'subscription' (a 6.0% match share), with 13 of those matches occurring in Evernote reviews. [S36](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S36)

Only 1 review out of the 300 matched the keyword 'paywall' (a 0.33% match share), which was a 5-star review for Todoist praising the absence of a paywall. [S20](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S20) [S37](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S37)

Evernote users report severe frustration with annual subscription costs rising to between $155 and $250 per year. [S8](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S8) [S16](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S16)

Sampled Evernote reviewers complain about intrusive, unskippable ads and promotional videos that interrupt note reading. [S7](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S7) [S12](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S12)

Notion users report billing confusion and an inability to upgrade to team or business plans mid-cycle when subscribed through Apple. [S6](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S6) [S11](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S11)

In contrast, Todoist users in the sample express appreciation for the app's free tier, noting that core features are not locked behind a paywall. [S20](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S20)

## What Higher-Rated Reviews Value

Across the 300 pooled reviews, the keyword 'love' matched in 42 reviews (14.0% match share), with 20 of those matches occurring in 5-star reviews. [S38](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S38)

The keyword 'best' matched in 27 reviews (9.0% match share), with 24 of those matches occurring in 5-star reviews. [S39](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S39)

Highly-rated Notion reviews value the app's deep customizability and its ability to act as a centralized database for organizing life and business workflows. [S21](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S21) [S26](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S26) [S27](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S27)

Highly-rated Todoist reviews highlight the app's effectiveness in reducing mental clutter, managing ADHD, and building habits. [S20](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S20) [S31](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S31) [S32](/api/reports/f17878315b5f420aaf114fbbcedb5575/sources/S32)

## What the data cannot establish

- The analysis is based on a bounded sample of 100 reviews per app from the US App Store RSS feed and does not represent the entire global user base.
- Keyword matching relies on token occurrences rather than semantic intent, and match shares do not reflect total complaint or satisfaction rates.
- The Mendeley corpus was excluded from app-specific comparisons due to a lack of app identifiers, dates, and storefront metadata.

## Questions to investigate next

- Conduct a broader longitudinal study using a larger dataset of App Store reviews to track sentiment changes following specific pricing updates.
- Analyze user feedback from other storefronts outside the US to determine if subscription and paywall complaints vary by region.
- Investigate the technical integration of Apple in-app purchases with third-party SaaS billing systems to address subscription upgrade friction.

### App Metadata & Baseline Subscription Structures (Developer Claims)

*   **Notion: Notes, Tasks, AI** (ID: `1232780281`) [S2]
    *   *Pricing Model:* Free-to-download with freemium structure. Offers a robust free tier for personal notes/docs and template access, alongside paid tiers (such as Notion Plus and Team plans) and optional AI add-ons [S2]. 
    *   *Developer Description:* Positioned as an AI-powered all-in-one workspace for writing, task/project management, and team collaboration [S2].
*   **Evernote: AI Notes & Notebook** (ID: `281796108`) [S3]
    *   *Pricing Model:* Freemium model with restricted free tier limits (e.g., device caps) and high-cost annual paid subscription tiers (such as Personal/Professional plans) [S3, S8, S10, S16].
    *   *Developer Description:* Marketed as a "second brain" capturing multi-format notes, web clippings, documents, and integrating semantic AI search [S3].
*   **Todoist: To Do List & Calendar** (ID: `572688855`) [S4]
    *   *Pricing Model:* Freemium model providing core task management and recurring schedules on its free tier, with optional paid upgrades for advanced professional power features [S4, S20].
    *   *Developer Description:* A task manager bridging personal and professional productivity featuring natural language quick-add, cross-platform sync, and flexible list/board/calendar views [S4].

---

### Identified Review Complaints & Positive Valuations

*Note: Keyword matches represent text token hits in sampled US reviews (denominator = 100 per app sample), not exhaustive population-wide prevalence.*

#### 1. Evernote
*   **Subscription & Paywall Complaints:** Evernote encounters severe pushback regarding aggressive paywalls, aggressive promotional popups, and dramatic year-over-year price escalation [S5, S7, S8, S10, S12, S16]. Users report annual subscription costs scaling up toward $155–$250/year [S8, S16]. Review complaints cite intrusive unskippable AI and upgrade ads interrupting note reading [S7, S12], as well as device-sync restrictions on free tiers [S10].
    *   *Examples:* 
        *   *"Prices have also skyrocketed—several times higher than a few years ago. I’m not paying for that."* (1-star) [S5]
        *   *"...having messages and videos about the subscription every time I try to open my note is too intrusive and time wasting."* (1-star) [S7]
        *   *"...the free version is a complete joke and it is constantly hounding you and trying to trick you..."* (1-star) [S16]
*   **Higher-Rated / Positive Valuations:** Higher-rated reviews appreciate long-standing historical utility, formatting structure, robust multi-device syncing, and flexible notebooks [S14, S17]. 
    *   *Note on evidence:* In the sampled US reviews for Evernote, 1- and 2-star complaints heavily dominate the discussion around pricing, whereas positive reviews emphasize legacy utility and core note-taking capabilities.

#### 2. Notion
*   **Subscription & Paywall Complaints:** Complaints center on subscription management friction (especially billing discrepancies when subscribing via Apple in-app purchases versus team accounts) and reliability glitches [S6, S11]. 
    *   *Examples:*
        *   *"I purchased a full year of Notion Plus for $119.99 through Apple... The app repeatedly displays confusing information about my subscription..."* (1-star) [S6]
        *   *"...you can’t upgrade your subscription! I signed up through Apple and now I want to bring on two other people to my 'business' subscription. You can’t do it!!!"* (3-star) [S11]
*   **Higher-Rated / Positive Valuations:** High-rating reviews (5-star) heavily praise Notion's deep customizability, all-in-one flexibility for life/business organization, database connections, and AI integrations [S21, S26, S27].
    *   *Examples:*
        *   *"I use Notion every day to keep my life organized... I love how customizable everything is..."* (5-star) [S21]
        *   *"...it’s so deeply customizable that I got basically hooked on it... makes my life so much easier."* (5-star) [S26]

#### 3. Todoist
*   **Subscription & Paywall Complaints:** Subscription complaints are virtually absent in the sampled US reviews; instead, users frequently celebrate the generosity of the free tier [S20].
    *   *Examples:*
        *   *"The free tier has worked well for me, and I really appreciate not having necessary features behind a paywall."* (5-star) [S20]
*   **Higher-Rated / Positive Valuations:** 5-star reviewers praise Todoist's clean interface, natural language quick-add, reliable cross-platform sync (desktop and mobile), and effectiveness for managing neurodivergence (like ADHD) and complex academic/business projects [S20, S23, S24].
    *   *Examples:*
        *   *"...this app has been a LIFESAVER. It clears up so much mental clutter to just immediately put tasks and reminders into my inbox..."* (5-star) [S20]
        *   *"I love the coordinated list which is accessible and actionable from both my desktop browser and the app on my phone."* (5-star) [S24]

---

### Data Notes & Limitations
*   **Observed Facts:** App Store metadata and pricing tiers as returned by Apple Search API [S2, S3, S4].
*   **Reported Complaints:** User grievances extracted from bounded Apple customer review RSS samples for US storefronts. Keyword matching counts reflect sample occurrences and should not be generalized to all global users.
*   **Suggested Improvements:** Mentioned across reviews include adding iPhone split-screen support (Notion) [S21], separate standalone notes sections (Todoist) [S23], and removing unskippable AI popups (Evernote) [S12].
*   **Limitations:** Review samples capture only a fraction of public feedback. Mendeley corpus data was excluded from app-specific comparisons due to lack of app identifiers.

### Overview of Identified US Reviews & Denominators
Based on the stored Apple customer-review RSS sample (300 total reviews across Notion, Evernote, and Todoist, with 100 per app), we examine keyword-match counts against the 300-review denominator [S36, S38, S39]. 

*Note: Keyword matching relies on token occurrences rather than semantic intent, and keyword-match share does not reflect total complaint prevalence.*

---

### Recurring Subscription and Paywall Complaints

#### 1. Evernote
* **Recurrent Themes:** Evernote generates the highest volume of subscription-related pushback in the sample. Users frequently cite steep, multi-year price inflation (moving from free or low-cost to over $150/year) [S8], aggressive unskippable AI and upgrade popups that interrupt workflows [S7, S12], and reduced device limits on free accounts that force paid upgrades [S10].
* **Example Quotes:** 
  * *"Prices have also skyrocketed—several times higher than a few years ago. I’m not paying for that. I’ve moved all my notes elsewhere and canceled my subscription."* [S5]
  * *"Having messages and videos about the subscription every time I try to open my note is too intrusive and time wasting."* [S7]

#### 2. Notion
* **Recurrent Themes:** Notion complaints center around subscription management friction (e.g., being unable to upgrade or add business seat members mid-cycle when subscribed via Apple) [S6, S11] and billing confusion [S6].
* **Example Quote:** 
  * *"I signed up through Apple and now I want to bring on two other people to my 'business' subscription. You can’t do it!!! I have to wait for my current subscription to expire..."* [S11]

#### 3. Todoist
* **Recurrent Themes:** Todoist receives very few subscription or paywall complaints in this sample. In higher-rated reviews, users explicitly commend the generosity of the free tier and the absence of aggressive paywalls blocking core functionality [S20].

---

### What Higher-Rated Reviews (4–5 Stars) Value

Higher-rated reviewers highlight flexibility, organization, and peace of mind:
* **Customization & Centralization:** Notion users value deep customizability, treating the app as a single "source-of-truth" database for home, school, and business workflows [S21, S27].
* **Habit Building & ADHD / Mental Clarity:** Todoist users frequently praise its natural language capture and recurring task structures for alleviating mental clutter and managing ADHD or academic schedules [S20, S31].
* **Reliable Cross-Platform Sync:** Users across Todoist and Notion value the seamless transition between desktop browsers and mobile apps [S24].

---

### Keyword-Match Counts & Denominators

Across the **300-review pooled denominator** (100 reviews per app), keyword matches (using ANY-token OR matching on the identified corpus) are as follows:

* **'love':** 42 matches out of 300 total reviews (**14.0%** match share; spans ratings 1–5, with 20 matches in 5-star reviews) [S38].
* **'best':** 27 matches out of 300 total reviews (**9.0%** match share; spans ratings 1–5, with 24 matches in 5-star reviews) [S39].
* **'subscription':** 18 matches out of 300 total reviews (**6.0%** match share; predominantly concentrated in 1-star to 3-star reviews for Evernote and Notion) [S36].
* **'paywall':** 1 match out of 300 total reviews (**0.33%** match share) [S37].

---

### Limitations & Research Notes
* **Observed Facts:** App metadata and review records exist within a bounded storefront sample (Apple RSS) and a historical corpus (Mendeley). 
* **Reported Complaints:** Evernote users report intrusive upgrade ads and sharp price increases [S7, S8]; Notion users report subscription-management friction via Apple billing [S6, S11].
* **Suggested Improvements:** Evernote users request less intrusive interfaces; Notion users request better in-app plan adjustments and side-by-side iPad/iPhone windowing [S11, S21].
* **Limitations:** Tool budgets restricted deep sub-keyword lookups for terms like 'worth' or 'organize'. Review samples represent vocal subsets rather than randomized user censuses.

report.title: Subscription Models and Value Propositions: Notion, Evernote, and Todoist

summary.text: A comparative analysis of sampled US App Store reviews reveals distinct user experiences and monetization friction points across Notion, Evernote, and Todoist.
Evernote faces significant user pushback regarding steep price increases and intrusive upgrade prompts.
Notion users report subscription management friction when billing is handled through Apple in-app purchases.
Todoist receives praise for its generous free tier, with highly-rated reviews emphasizing its organizational utility.

claims.text: In the pooled sample of 300 reviews across the three apps, 18 reviews matched the keyword 'subscription' (a 6.0% match share), with 13 of those matches occurring in Evernote reviews.
Only 1 review out of the 300 matched the keyword 'paywall' (a 0.33% match share), which was a 5-star review for Todoist praising the absence of a paywall.
Evernote users report severe frustration with annual subscription costs rising to between $155 and $250 per year.
Sampled Evernote reviewers complain about intrusive, unskippable ads and promotional videos that interrupt note reading.
Notion users report billing confusion and an inability to upgrade to team or business plans mid-cycle when subscribed through Apple.
In contrast, Todoist users in the sample express appreciation for the app's free tier, noting that core features are not locked behind a paywall.
Across the 300 pooled reviews, the keyword 'love' matched in 42 reviews (14.0% match share), with 20 of those matches occurring in 5-star reviews.
The keyword 'best' matched in 27 reviews (9.0% match share), with 24 of those matches occurring in 5-star reviews.
Highly-rated Notion reviews value the app's deep customizability and its ability to act as a centralized database for organizing life and business workflows.
Highly-rated Todoist reviews highlight the app's effectiveness in reducing mental clutter, managing ADHD, and building habits.

limitations: The analysis is based on a bounded sample of 100 reviews per app from the US App Store RSS feed and does not represent the entire global user base.
Keyword matching relies on token occurrences rather than semantic intent, and match shares do not reflect total complaint or satisfaction rates.
The Mendeley corpus was excluded from app-specific comparisons due to a lack of app identifiers, dates, and storefront metadata.
next_steps: Conduct a broader longitudinal study using a larger dataset of App Store reviews to track sentiment changes following specific pricing updates.
Analyze user feedback from other storefronts outside the US to determine if subscription and paywall complaints vary by region.
Investigate the technical integration of Apple in-app purchases with third-party SaaS billing systems to address subscription upgrade friction.

data.name: Evernote: AI Notes & Notebook
data.description:
Evernote is your second brain — the place to keep everything that matters and find it again the moment you need it.

"…an invaluable tool for organizing a messy digital life." — The New York Times

Capture a thought, a to-do, a photo, or a whole project, then let Evernote help you organize it, make sense of it, transcribe a meeting or tidy up a rough draft, and bring it back exactly when it counts. From the first spark of an idea to the finished plan, it all lives in one calm, searchable place — at work, at home, and everywhere in between.

CAPTURE ANYTHING
Jot a quick note, build a checklist, save a photo, an email or a PDF, or clip an article from the web before it disappears. Type it out, write by hand, snap a picture, or record a voice memo — whatever's fastest in the moment. Your ideas land in one place, ready when you are, so nothing gets lost on a sticky note or buried in your inbox.

STAY ORGANIZED, EFFORTLESSLY
Sort notes into notebooks and add tags, or just start writing and let structure follow. Group related notes together, pin the ones you reach for most, and keep work, school, and life neatly apart — without spending your day tidying up. Evernote keeps things in order so you can stay focused on the thinking.

FIND WHAT YOU NEED, FAST
Search across everything you've saved — including the text inside your images and PDFs. Ask in plain language and Semantic Search surfaces the right note, even when you can't remember the exact words or where you put it. The more you save, the more useful it becomes.

MEET YOUR AI ASSISTANT
Your AI Assistant clears away the busywork so you can stay in the thinking, working quietly alongside you. Record a conversation and Evernote AI transcribes and summarizes it for you; AI Transcription turns audio, images, and video into text; and AI Edit cleans up a rough draft, shortens it, or changes the tone while keeping it in your own voice.

PLAN YOUR DAY
Add due dates, reminders, and to-dos right inside your notes, so the next step is always clear and nothing slips through the cracks. Check things off as you go and keep momentum without switching apps.

WORK EVERYWHERE
Your notes sync automatically across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and the web — start on one device and pick up right where you left off on another. Evernote works offline too, so you're never locked out of your own ideas, even when you're far from a signal.

FOR WORK, SCHOOL, AND LIFE
- Plan projects, prep meetings, and keep every detail in one place.
- Take lecture notes, organize research, and study smarter for exams.
- Save recipes, plan trips, track goals, and remember the little things that matter.
- Keep a journal, draft your next big idea, and capture inspiration whenever it strikes.

"Its magic lies in its flexibility." — PCMag

However you think, and whatever you're working on, Evernote helps you remember everything and get it done. Capture today's idea — and find it the moment you need it.
